result.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration
result.summary: Image restoration remains a fundamental challenge in low-level vision, requiring methods that handle diverse degradations while preserving scene structures and details. We revisit classical Retinex theory and propose a Generalized Retinex formulation that extends the illumination-reflectance decomposition into a Retinex-inspired content-environment factorization prior for image restoration. The key idea is to restore images using two learned factors: a content-dominant response (generalized reflectance) capturing scene properties and an environment-side response (generalized illumination) encoding task-dependent variations associated with the observed degradations. Based on this formulation, we develop GRUN (Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network), a MAP-guided deep unfolding framework that alternates reflectance restoration, illumination estimation, and progressive degradation inference across K stages with degradation-conditioned proximal operators. We further introduce a Degradation-aware Coupling Regularizer (DCR) that combines mutual information minimization, gradient decorrelation, and scale anchoring to promote complementary content-environment factor representations. Experiments on seven image restoration tasks, including denoising, dehazing, deraining, low-light enhancement, deblurring, underwater enhancement, and backlit enhancement, demonstrate competitive results on multiple benchmarks using the same architecture with task-specific weights. Moreover, the proposed Generalized Retinex design can be integrated into existing restoration methods, demonstrating its cross-architecture applicability. Code will be released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将经典 Retinex 的照明-反射分解推广为内容-环境因子先验，提出 MAP 引导的 K 阶段深度展开网络 GRUN，交替执行反射恢复、照明估计与退化推断，并用结合互信息最小化、梯度去相关与尺度锚定的耦合正则促使两因子互补。
AI.relevance_reason: 其分阶段交替状态更新与防止因子坍缩的解耦正则，可能为 LVR 中推理状态与视觉细节表征的分离及信息坍缩诊断提供可核查线索；但属像素级复原任务，与多模态推理无直接联系。
